title: Rafael and the Thorn Anew
premise: Vesper Eastwick, the last oath-bound swordspeaker whose blade speaks the names of the dead it has avenged, has spent years hiding her gift in the smuggler's roads of the Thornfell mountains. When the crown's witch-hunters begin burning anyone with the gift, Vesper is forced to guide a captured young speaker named Rafael to the capital — until she learns he is bait meant to draw out survivors of Thornfell, a country erased from maps and memory by royal decree. Betraying her crown oath to protect him, Vesper seeks the Door of Anew, a passage said to lead out of a nation that officially no longer exists. In the climax she must speak her own true name through her sword — surrendering every memory that made her — so Rafael and the last Thornfell exiles can pass through before winter seals the mountains; she survives, nameless but free, choosing to rebuild herself from loyalty rather than truth.
about_author: Mirabel Eastwick is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes about borders, oaths, and the people who live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: The Blade That Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She guides contraband salt through a frozen pass, using her swordspeech only once to bury a dead courier's name. Establishes her gift, her secrecy, and the ache of carrying memories not her own. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Proclamation at Grayford
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the market town of Grayford, criers announce the crown's hunt for gifted speakers; a neighbor is taken in daylight. Vesper burns her false papers and flees north. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Boy in the Cage Wagon
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ambushed on the high road, she finds a crown convoy transporting Rafael, a terrified boy whose whispered words make stone bloom. She kills his escort in a blur of spoken steel. Emotional beat: reluctant rescue becoming commitment.

chapters.title: What Rafael Knows
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Hiding in a shepherd's bothy, Rafael reveals he was told to walk the Thornfell roads until someone found him — he doesn't know by whom. Vesper realizes he is bait. Emotional beat: trust built through shared hunger.

chapters.title: Oathbound
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback chapter: how Vesper swore her crown oath after Thornfell fell, and what the oath-magic does to those who break it. Present-day: the oath begins pulling her toward the capital. Emotional beat: dread of a debt coming due.

chapters.title: Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The pair shelter in Hollowmere, a village where no one can say which country they were born in. An old woman recognizes Rafael's accent as Thornfell-born. Emotional beat: uncanny tenderness among the memory-broken.

chapters.title: The Witch-Hunter's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Hunter-Captain Serane Vole interrogates a captured smuggler who describes Vesper exactly. Serane closes the mountain passes. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace.

chapters.title: Roads That No Longer Exist
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper leads Rafael onto smuggler roads cut through land the crown unmade — bridges over valleys that are 'not there,' villages struck from records. Her gift lets the sword remember their names. Emotional beat: wonder braided with mourning.

chapters.title: The Exiles of Thornfell
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. They find a hidden colony of Thornfell survivors led by Maren Ostwick, who claims to know the way to the Door of Anew. Maren tests Vesper's loyalty with questions about the fall. Emotional beat: cautious homecoming.

chapters.title: Maren's Price
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Maren agrees to guide them only if Vesper surrenders her sword — the colony fears its speech will draw hunters. Vesper refuses; Rafael offers himself as hostage instead. Emotional beat: loyalty colliding with survival.

chapters.title: Serane's Offer
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Serane corners Vesper alone and offers pardon for Rafael's capture, revealing the hunt's true purpose: the crown fears the Door of Anew more than any speaker. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: First Snow, First Blood
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Hunters raid the colony. Rafael's gift erupts, saving children but revealing him; Maren is mortally wounded and gives Vesper a broken map-stone pointing to the Door. Emotional beat: guilt and inheritance.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With the pass closing, the group races the season up the spine of the Thornfells. A member freezes; Vesper speaks his name into the sword rather than let him die unmourned. Emotional beat: grief as fuel.

chapters.title: What the Sword Says
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael overhears the sword whisper Vesper's buried memories — including that she helped burn the records of Thornfell under her old oath. He confronts her. Emotional beat: betrayal cracking hard-won trust.

chapters.title: Split at the Saddle
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Rafael runs toward Serane's camp, believing surrender may save the others. Vesper chooses to follow him rather than reach the Door alone. Emotional beat: love choosing the harder road.

chapters.title: Camp of Ash Lanterns
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Rafael reaches the hunters' camp; Serane, herself secretly gifted, hesitates. Vesper walks in unarmed to bargain. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing each other's cages.

chapters.title: The Door of Anew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The map-stone opens a seam in a glacier wall: a door standing free in snow, older than the country it exits. Serane arrives with Rafael at spear-point. Emotional beat: terrible stillness before the choice.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Whole
chapters.summary: Climax, Vesper's POV. To open the Door, a speaker must give their true name and all memories bound to it. Vesper speaks hers through the sword, unraveling her past — including her oath — as hunters close in. Emotional beat: sacrifice as self-erasure.

chapters.title: Through
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The Door holds open only while Vesper's name lasts. Rafael drags the wounded Serane through against her orders; the exiles cross; the Door seals behind them into blank ice. Emotional beat: desperate gratitude.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Beyond the Door lies Thornfell as it was remembered, not as it was — imperfect, half-invented, sustained by exile memory. Serane must decide whether to enforce a crown law over a country that exists nowhere else. Emotional beat: dislocation and dawning freedom.

chapters.title: Stranger at the Hearth
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A nameless woman arrives at the settlement's hearth, carrying a silent sword. Rafael knows her gait if not her face. Emotional beat: hope trembling on recognition.

chapters.title: Thorn Anew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Without memories, Vesper begins again: learning names, seasons, kindnesses. She re-swears an oath of her own choosing — to Rafael and the rebuilt Thornfell — and the sword speaks one new word: her chosen name. Emotional beat: quiet, earned rebirth.
